title: The SwiftUI app lifecycle: App, Scene and the view hierarchy

videos.script: Lesson 1's program ran from its first line to its last, and then it ended. An app does not. {{app}} A SwiftUI app is a value that describes the app. SwiftUI is the program that runs it, and keeps it running. {{scenes}} Inside the app are scenes. On an iPhone, one window. On an iPad, perhaps two, from the same declaration, and each with its own state. {{phase}} And every scene is in one of three phases. Active, inactive, or in the background. On a phone, people do not close apps. They leave them. From the background, iOS may end the process without a word. {{machine}} So the app has to decide when to save, and when to refresh. You write that decision in plain Swift, test it, and watch the first version fail. {{tree}} Then the tree of views the planner will grow, with its four screens. {{restore}} And what has to survive when the app comes back from nothing.
